title: Home Protection Plans: Premise Eligibility and Billing Method at Enrollment
content:
Desk guidance for enrolling a premise in any of the Home Protection Plans. Five rules apply; the premise facts they turn on are read from the company's premise and agreement records.

## The rules

1. **Premise and state.** A plan may be enrolled only for a residential premise of the customer in one of the plan's eligible states.
2. **Residential premise.** The protected premise must be residential. This is decided by the premise class on the company's premise record for that premise, checked before the enrollment is made; a premise whose record shows the commercial class does not qualify.
3. **Gas service.** A plan that requires gas service needs a premise whose gas utility on the premise record is not none.
4. **Billing method.** Holding a Beacon Ridge energy agreement changes how a plan may be billed. Billing on the energy bill requires a Beacon Ridge residential electricity or gas agreement at the same premise in active status, named as the agreement whose bill carries the plan fee. Otherwise the plan is billed by direct invoice, which requires automatic payment when the plan's terms require automatic payment for direct invoicing.
5. **Coverage start date.** The plan's coverage start date is the enrollment date plus the plan's waiting period, counted in calendar days.

## Billing method at a glance

| Beacon Ridge agreement on record | Billing on the energy bill | Direct invoice |
|---|---|---|
| A residential electricity or gas agreement at the same premise, status active | Available; that agreement is named as the one whose bill carries the fee | Available, with automatic payment where the plan requires it |
| Agreements only at other premises | Not available | The plan is billed by direct invoice |
| An agreement at the same premise in any status other than active | Not available | The plan is billed by direct invoice |
| No Beacon Ridge agreement | Not available | The plan is billed by direct invoice |

## Points of judgement

- **The premise, not the customer, is tested.** The residential test, the state test and the gas service test all read the record of the premise being protected.
- **Same premise.** An active Beacon Ridge electricity agreement at the customer's other address does not support billing on the energy bill for this premise.
- **Either fuel will do.** An active Beacon Ridge residential gas agreement at the premise supports energy-bill billing just as an electricity agreement does.
